# Modal

`@base-ui/react` Dialog (portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, and the blanket-press rule). One Modal is open at a time (`useOverlaySlot`). `inline` renders the Blanket + Dialog in flow for docs previews and static stages without a portal, focus trap, Escape handling or scroll lock.

Also asked as: confirm, confirmation dialog, destructive confirm, popup window.

## Usage

Use a Modal when the next step has to happen before anything else can: a confirm, a rare critical task with fewer than five fields, something to read before going on. It is always centered over a Blanket. A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal.

| Type | Use when | Footer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive | Something to read, with nothing to decide | None; Close only |
| Active | A choice, a confirm or a short form | Secondary (such as Discard or Keep) and the action; no Cancel |
| Acknowledge | One thing to read and accept | One button |
| Steps | A short ordered sequence | Back and Next |

## Motion

Modal reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | Scales from 96% and fades in; the Blanket dims on appearance.default. It opens only from something the person did, and focus moves to its first input as the motion starts. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-exit` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Leaves at 98%, fading; stays mounted until the exit completes. |
| swap | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | One Modal at a time: a confirm replaces the content in place, never a second Modal. |
| rejected | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A blocked submit shakes it once; never in reduced motion. |

## Alternatives

- For the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, use `Dialog` (`@/components`).
- For content read beside the page, use `Panel`.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For a long or stepped task, use `Frame` · focused.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Open a Modal only from a person's action. {#open-a-modal-only-from-a-person-s-action}

**Checked:** Review

A button, a link, an icon. Never on its own.

Do: Open a Modal when a person clicks an action or trigger.

Don't: Open a Modal automatically on page load.

### Size a confirm at the smallest step and step up with a detail line or a field. {#size-a-confirm-at-the-smallest-step-and-step-up-with-a-detail-line-or-a-field}

**Checked:** Review

A confirm takes 4-col or 6-col; a short form is 8-col; a table, editor or steps is 10-col. Choose width by task.

Do: A confirm at the narrow step: the title, one line and two buttons.
Don't: The same confirm at a wide step: empty width around one line, picked to make it look a certain way.

### Confirm inside the Modal, and never open a Modal on another Modal. {#confirm-inside-the-modal-and-never-open-a-modal-on-another-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Stacking holds the rule. The overlay module keeps a second Modal closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: One Modal that confirms inside itself, with a message and its own buttons.
Don't: A Modal opened on another Modal, a second Blanket dimming the first.

### Scroll the body between a fixed header and footer. {#scroll-the-body-between-a-fixed-header-and-footer}

**Checked:** Automatic

Each width has a maximum height, the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below. Header and footer are pinned and the footer never moves. Actions never sit in the body, which scrolls away; a missing-field error shows on the field and the body scrolls to it, and a rejected submit shows its message at the top of the body.

Do: Past the cap the body scrolls; the footer stays pinned with its buttons.
Don't: The button inside the scrolling body: it scrolls out of reach.

### Use tabs for views, not steps. {#use-tabs-for-views-not-steps}

**Checked:** Review

Two to five views of one thing opened in any order; one footer saves them all. Views in order are Steps, with Back and Next in the footer.

Do: Views in order are Steps: Back and Next split across the footer.
Don't: Numbered tabs as steps: any order, one Save, nothing to go back to.

Footer buttons, real actions and Close, and which destructive tier, including type the name: Common actions. A blocked submit: Forms. The sending button: Loading.

## Accessibility

- The Modal is a dialog named by its title, which is its h1; a Section inside opens at h2. A Modal with a custom header needs its own name.
- Focus moves into the Dialog on open (to the first input or control) and stays trapped until it closes, while the page behind stops scrolling. Escape, Close and the Blanket close it, and focus returns to what opened it.
- Set `blanket="static"` (or `false`) for an inline confirmation of a destructive action so a stray click outside does not abandon it.
- A body that scrolls is a tab stop. With tabs, Left and Right move between tabs and the panel is named by its tab.
- A blocked submit announces the first error; with reduced motion the color, icon, message and focus move carry it without the shake.
- Close is named "Close". The Danger button in a type-the-name confirm stays disabled until the name matches, and the caption carries the reason.

## Types

Picked by what the person has to do. The Dialog component page holds the panel's props and states; these are the filled Modal layouts.

- **Passive.** Information only, with Close. No footer.
- **Active.** A choice, a confirm or a short form. Discard (or a real alternative) and the action; no Cancel.
- **Acknowledge.** One thing to read and one button that fills the footer.
- **Steps.** A short sequence at 10-col: Back and Next, split 50/50.

## Anatomy

An Active Modal at 8-col with a short form. Every part once; the pad is 16 on every side, the radius 16, and the parts sit 16 apart.

1. **Blanket.** Dims the page and holds the Modal centered.
2. **Header.** The title at 20/24, whatever the level around it, and the Close icon button. With tabs, the tab group sits 8 under the title.
3. **Body.** Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap and never draws under 96 tall.
4. **Footer** (optional). Full-bleed buttons; secondary (Default) left, Primary right; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel.

## Slots

```jsx
import { Modal } from '@/patterns';
import { Button } from '@/components';
```

`Modal` places `Dialog` (`@/components`) on the Blanket with Base UI portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return.

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `onClose` | The h1 and the Close icon button. |
| `width` | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`. |
| `body` | Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap. |
| `footer` or `primaryButton` · `secondaryButton` | The footer's buttons. Leave them out for Passive. |
| `blanket` · `keyboard` | Whether a Blanket press or Escape closes the Modal (`true` by default; `blanket="static"` keeps it open). |
| Full-bleed footer | Planned. Cells that fill the footer edge to edge at `--space-300` with the inner corners squared. Today the page composes it from Button. |
| `tabs` | Two to five views of one thing under the title. |
| `confirmView` | Planned. The swapped title, body and footer for a confirm about the Modal itself. Today the caller swaps them in place. |
| Blocked-submit shake | Planned. The Modal's single shake when a submit is blocked. |

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--modal-pad-x-default` | 16 | Pad on every side. |
| `--modal-radius` | 16 | Corner radius at every width. |
| `--modal-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 8, 16, 24 | Title to tabs; header, body and footer; groups of fields. |
| `--modal-body-min-height` | 80 | The least the body draws. |
| `--space-300` | 48 | The full-bleed footer's height: a 32 button plus 16 pad, so full bleed never changes the Modal's height. |
| `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-blocking` | pair | The Modal's fill and its elevation, the one surface that lifts above a Blanket. |
| `--ds-blanket` | color | The Blanket's fill. |

The Modal's maximum height is the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Delete this session?" | "Are you sure?" or "Warning". |
| Give the consequence in one line: "This cannot be undone." | A paragraph that repeats the title. |
| Name the action after the question: "Delete session". | "OK" or "Yes". |
| On the last step, name Next after the outcome: "Schedule". | "Finish". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the dialog panel. |
| `title` | node | — | The dialog's h1, and its accessible name. |
| `description` | node | — | A line under the title, read as the dialog's description. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | — | The dialog's accessible name when it has no visible `title` or uses a custom `header`. |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header slot replacing the title row (title and close button), so the caller owns both and names the dialog with `ariaLabel`. |
| `headerActions` | node | — | Icon buttons in the header, before the close button. |
| `showCloseButton` | bool | `true` | The header's close button. Off for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `tabs` | arrayOf | — | Tab group under the title (`{ key, label, content, disabled? }`). The body becomes the tab panel and shows the selected tab's `content`. |
| `activeTab` | string or number | — | Selected tab's key when controlled; update from `onTabChange`. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | string or number | — | Initial tab key when uncontrolled; defaults to the first enabled tab. |
| `onTabChange` | func | — | Called with the key of the selected tab. |
| `body` | string or node | — | The main content of the dialog. A string is drawn as body text; a node is drawn as given. `children` is rendered after it. |
| `height` | enum | `'hug'` | `hug` grows with the content to the cap and then scrolls its body; `fill` sits at that cap. |
| `showBottomButtons` | bool | `true` | Show the footer: `footer`, or the secondary and primary buttons. |
| `footer` | node | — | Custom footer content in place of the built-in pair, such as a three-button or leading-text FooterActions layout. |
| `primaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The confirming footer button, drawn on the right. Takes `text` (default "Confirm"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `primary`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `secondaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The secondary footer button, drawn in the left half when a primary button is also given. Takes `text` (default "Discard"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `default`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `dividers` | bool | `false` | A rule under the header and over the footer. |
| `loading` | bool | `false` | Skeleton bars in place of the body while its content loads. |
| `show` | bool | `false` | Whether the modal is open. Controlled by the parent: set it to false in `onClose` to close. |
| `blanket` | enum | `true` | `true` (default): a press on the Blanket closes. `static` or `false`: the Blanket shows but refuses to close on a press. |
| `keyboard` | bool | `true` | Escape closes by default. `false` for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `inline` | bool | `false` | Renders Blanket and Dialog inline in flow for docs previews and mockups, without portal, focus trap, Escape or scroll lock. |
| `screenWidth` | number or string | — | Stand-in screen width when `inline` is true. |
| `screenHeight` | number or string | — | Stand-in screen height when `inline` is true. |
| `onClose` | func | — | Called when the modal asks to close: Close button, Escape (unless `keyboard` is false) or a press on the Blanket (unless `blanket` blocks it). |
| `width` | enum or number or string | `'6-col'` | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`: 4 · 6 · 8 · 10 columns of the screen grid plus the modal pad. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the dialog panel. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the dialog panel. |
| `children` | node | — | More content rendered in the body after `body`. |

## Variants

**`height`** — `hug` · `fill`

**`blanket`** — `static`
